question: Why is no average power consumed in a purely inductive or purely capacitive AC circuit? Give reason.

options.A: Average power is zero because the current is zero throughout the cycle.
options.B: Average power is zero because the resistance of an ideal inductor or capacitor is infinite.
options.C: In a pure inductor or capacitor, $\phi=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $P=VI\cos\phi=0$. Energy is alternately stored and returned during each cycle.
options.D: Average power is zero because voltage and current have a phase difference of $\pi$.
